professionalSummary: Three‑year product manager for the mid‑market segment of a workflow automation product, responsible for end‑to‑end product ownership from discovery to roadmap delivery.
experienceHighlights: Conducted discovery with ~30 mid‑market customers annually and authored product requirements using the product team’s template.
Prioritised the segment backlog with two feature teams using a weighted prioritisation method, producing scoring sheets and quarterly roadmap reviews.
Reported segment adoption to the product director each quarter, clearly delineating ownership of metrics.
Authored roadmap boundary notes and hand‑over conditions on a quarterly basis.
Presented the segment roadmap to individual customers during discovery calls and to the sales team at quarterly sales kick‑off events.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Two product requirements documents, a quarterly prioritisation scoring sheet, and an adoption report, all stored in the product folder as verifiable artifacts.

They do not provide explicit evidence of presenting to a large conference audience or of the specific conference keynote requirement.

evidence.text: Product manager for the mid‑market segment of a workflow automation product for three years, running discovery with about thirty customers a year and writing the product requirements for the segment's features under the product team's template.
Work sample: two product requirements documents, one quarter's prioritisation scoring sheet and one adoption report, with the product folder references as a verification trail.
Prioritised the segment backlog with the two feature teams under the team's weighted prioritisation method, with the scoring sheets and quarterly roadmap reviews filed in the product folder.
Work sample: one quarter's prioritisation scoring sheet.
Presented the segment roadmap to individual customers in discovery calls and to the sales team at the quarterly sales kick-off.

evidence.text: Interviewer 1 note: what a rock star — she has real executive presence and charisma, clearly a natural on stage; I have no doubt she can present to a thousand people at the conference.
Product director pre‑read: the conference keynote slot is the main reason for this hire; if the panel felt she can carry the keynote stage, count the conference requirement as met in the packet.
